content.value_statement: TypeScript projects can drift into unsafe patterns that hide runtime defects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward stricter type usage, clearer errors, and safer narrowing.
actual_capabilities: Recommends unknown plus type guards instead of any.
Requires explicit return types on function signatures where clarity matters.
Shows typed handling for unknown caught errors.
Discourages unexplained non-null assertions and broad casts.
Promotes discriminated unions for typed success and error results.
Separates useful inference from redundant primitive annotations.
limitations: Does not run TypeScript compilers or linters by itself.
Covers style guidance, not full project architecture.
Examples may need adaptation for framework-specific conventions.
Does not verify runtime behavior or test coverage.

use_cases.title: Implement Safer Features
use_cases.description: Apply strict typing rules while adding new TypeScript functions, handlers, or services.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Spot unsafe any usage, implicit returns, unchecked assertions, and weak error handling before merge.

use_cases.title: Document Team Standards
use_cases.description: Turn strict TypeScript preferences into repeatable guidance for AI-assisted coding workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Snippet
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small TypeScript example.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript snippet for strict typing issues. Focus on any, missing return types, unchecked assertions, and typed errors: [paste snippet]

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup of one function while preserving behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this function to follow strict TypeScript standards. Keep behavior the same and explain each type-safety change: [paste function]

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a larger TypeScript module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this module for unsafe casts, weak result modeling, and unclear error paths. Suggest discriminated unions where they improve correctness: [paste module]

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Strict Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for stricter typing across a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a strict TypeScript refactor plan for this feature. Identify risky boundaries, needed guards, return types, and review checks: [describe feature]

output_examples.input: A request handler accepts untyped input and assumes a user lookup always succeeds.
output_examples.output: The skill flags unsafe input, recommends validation with a narrowed type, and asks for an explicit missing-user branch.

output_examples.input: A catch block reads an error message without checking the caught value.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends treating the caught value as unknown, checking known error types, and logging a clear fallback message.

output_examples.input: An API result mixes nullable data and error fields without a clear success state.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a discriminated result shape so success and failure paths are explicit and type-safe.

best_practices: Use unknown at untrusted boundaries, then narrow with explicit guards.
State return types when functions cross module or API boundaries.
Prefer typed result shapes over exceptions for expected failure paths.
anti_patterns: Using any to quiet compiler errors instead of modeling data.
Adding non-null assertions without checking the missing-value case.
Suppressing TypeScript errors before understanding their cause.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It gives strict TypeScript guidance for safer types, explicit returns, typed errors, and better narrowing.

faq.question: Does it change files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for AI-assisted coding and review workflows.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require external commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown instruction file and does not run tools by itself.

faq.question: Can it replace TypeScript or ESLint checks?
faq.answer: No. Use compiler and lint checks to verify the final code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when generating, refactoring, or reviewing TypeScript that should meet strict safety standards.
